current_bottleneck: 277c showed that learned retrieval is viable, but the change-only future target makes the similarity metric too level-free. The live bottleneck is now the retrieval target representation, not the retrieval family itself.
last_result_summary: Iteration 81 ran 277c-v0. It scored 3/11 overall, passing surface, block_ar, and cross_cell_correlation. The learned metric preserved surface validity and joint structure, but level KS collapsed to 0/25 and active MR stayed dead because the retrieval target encoded future changes without enough anchored level information.
next_step_recommendation: Implement 277d-v0: keep learned retrieval, but train it on a richer future target that includes both daily changes and cumulative displacement from the current state.
current_best_model: Archived baselines retain the overall 4/11 frontier. In the new two-level program, 277a, 277b, and 277c are the strongest deterministic Stage A results so far at 3/11, with retrieval clearly ahead of the learned smoothers.
current_best_note: Retrieval remains the active deterministic Stage A family. The next step is to enrich the learned retrieval target, not to abandon retrieval or add side mechanisms.
